conviction_note: Q3 was 70-86% pre-booked and lands at about the $2.27-2.29 consensus. The release turns on Q4-to-date bookings. Peers DHT, Okeanis and Teekay published record Q4 bookings 9-11 Nov and their stocks barely moved. FRO is down 22% in November on a 25-64% VLCC spot correction and Hormuz-deal headlines. A sold-down name gets a record Q4 booking, but that booking was telegraphed by peers who bought nothing on it, and puts are bid, so p_up 51 on a 4.5% absolute move. The findings sum to -0.25, a small negative from the spot correction and the Hormuz-corridor tail. Both measurements say there is no edge here, and the gap between them is noise.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 is mostly pre-booked and should land near consensus. At the 2026-08-28 Q2 release, Q3 VLCC days were 86% booked at $156,900/day, Suezmax 79% at $117,400 and LR2/Aframax 70% at $81,000, with management saying the full quarter would come in below those levels on ballast days. Against Q2 actuals ($152.7k/$111.5k/$92.4k) and two VLCCs sold in Aug/Sep, that points to an adjusted EPS of about $2.3-2.5 against the $2.27-2.29 consensus. The small upside is the 14-30% of open days fixed during the late-September spike: DHT's Q3 VLCC spot was $167.1k, and peers DHT and Okeanis beat Q3 consensus by 15% and 108%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 missed consensus ($2.61 against $2.74) and the stock rose about +0.5% to +1%. Q3 2025 missed by $0.05 and fell 6.7% over the week. On this line the stock reacts muted and mixed.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the bookings have been public since August and consensus sits right on them. The only unpriced part is the late-September fixing on open days. If that were priced, consensus would sit above $2.5, as it did not after the DHT/Okeanis beats.
findings.independence: DHT Q3 VLCC spot $167.1k/day and a 15% EPS beat (https://www.bairdmaritime.com/shipping/tankers/dht-holdings-third-quarter-profit). Teekay's Q3 Suezmax spot was $106.4k and LR2 $67.6k, both below FRO's bookings (https://www.bairdmaritime.com/shipping/tankers/teekay-tankers-net-income-falls). That cuts the LR2/Suezmax upside and is why the size is small.

findings.finding: FRO's Q4-to-date bookings, published in this release, will be a record far above Q3, going by same-quarter peers reported 9-11 Nov. DHT booked 68% of Q4 VLCC spot days at $579,900/day (9 Nov). Okeanis booked 48% of VLCC spot days at $688,800 and 60% of Suezmax days at $410,900 (11 Nov). Teekay booked Q4 Suezmax at $272,000 and Aframax/LR2 at $208,300 (11 Nov). FRO's Q3 levels were $157k/$117k/$81k. On FRO's fleet (40 VLCC, 19 Suezmax, 18 LR2) that implies a Q4 EPS several times the about $2.5 Q4 the stale FY consensus ($9.02) leaves room for. The peers' stocks did not move on the same disclosure: DHT was flat to +1.8%, Okeanis -0.3%.
findings.link: same spot markets in the same quarter: DHT and Okeanis trade VLCCs (FRO 40 VLCCs), Okeanis and Teekay trade Suezmax (FRO 19), Teekay trades Aframax/LR2 (FRO 18)
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FRO gives quarter-to-date bookings every print. Q2 2026's Q3 bookings ($157k against Q2 bookings of $181.7k) came with a +0.5-1% move. Peers this month: DHT about flat to +1.8% on $579.9k, Okeanis -0.3% on $688.8k. The market does not pay much for record forward bookings at a perceived peak.
findings.why_not_priced: The level is largely telegraphed by peers. What is not is FRO's own mix: its Q3 VLCC rate ($157k) trailed Okeanis ($269k) and DHT ($167k), so FRO's Gulf exposure and Q4 rate are unknown. Street FY numbers do not reflect it either ($9.02 on 1 Nov implies a Q4 near Q3). If it were priced, FY consensus would be $13+ and the stock would not sit 22% below its November high.
findings.independence: Okeanis: https://finviz.com/news/421910/okeanis-eco-tankers-doubles-consensus-and-locks-in-a-huge-q4-but-the-rate-peak-may-already-be-behind-it (2026-11-12). Teekay: https://www.bairdmaritime.com/shipping/tankers/teekay-tankers-net-income-falls (2026-11-11). Three different companies, so three independent documents, but one read-through.

findings.finding: The spot market corrected sharply after FRO last spoke. Gulf of Oman-China VLCC fell to about WS308 on 13 Nov, 64% below the WS841 record of 8 Oct (Reuters via gCaptain, 16 Nov). TD22 (US Gulf-China) was down 63.6% and TD3C earnings down 25% to about $1.06m/day. Several Suezmax/Aframax routes fell 50-70% in the week to 6 Nov, and Okeanis management put VLCC spot near $350k and Suezmax at $150-200k. FRO's open Q4 days and its Q1 2027 commentary will be priced off these lower levels.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observed on FRO's own prints. On equities, FRO is -22% in November while rates fell; Okeanis's cautious remarks on its print came with -0.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock fell 22% month to date. What is not priced is how cautiously management frames Q1 2027 on the call. If that were fully in, the stock would have stabilised and the skew would be flatter than +21.6.
findings.independence: https://cyprusshippingnews.com/2026/11/12/atlantic-tanker-earnings-fall-faster-than-gulf-earnings/ (Baltic via Signal Ocean, week to 6 Nov: TD22 -16.2% w/w, -34.9% from peak; Aframax TD19 -69.8%).

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's print came near the 52-week high with a muted +0.5-1%. No sold-down setup on FRO in the confirmed history.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown is driven by rates and Hormuz headlines, not by FRO-specific numbers. The positive skew says the market still pays for more downside, so this is a lean that cuts against the option market and is sized small. If the setup were priced as a relief candidate, puts would not be bid at +21.6.

findings.finding: Hormuz headline risk sits inside the one-day window. On 17 Nov Iran's foreign minister visited Oman to discuss maritime corridors, and Oman said it hoped a temporary Hormuz shipping corridor could be announced soon. The US-Iran track is stalled and attacks on tankers have increased. An announcement would hit tanker equities regardless of the print: tanker shares fell on earlier reopening headlines, DHT -3% on Iran's reopening offer.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: DHT about -3% on Iran's offer to reopen the strait (Motley Fool/Nasdaq). Lloyd's List reported FRO -2% on a Hormuz-traffic day.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a tail inside the window, partly in the put skew. The expected value is small, and a lean against the print happens only if the announcement lands on 20 Nov.
findings.independence: https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/why-dht-holdings-stock-dropped-today (DHT down on a reopening offer). This is a proxy: macro to company.

findings.finding: FRO has less Q4 spot leverage than its pure-spot peers. Barstad said VLCC revenue cover was 'slightly above 30%' (policy: about a third). Two newbuild VLCCs are on one-year charters at $120k/day, and two 2016 VLCCs on two- and three-year charters at $90k and $75k/day from August 2026. He conceded FRO fixed 'a little bit too early.' Fleet-wide Q4 earnings will trail what a $580k-$690k peer VLCC spot booking implies per ship.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction to cover levels observed.
findings.why_not_priced: It was disclosed in August, so the level is known. What is not settled is whether analysts mechanically apply peer spot rates to FRO's whole fleet.
findings.independence: The charter rates and dates are in the Q2 release: https://www.financialcontent.com/article/gnwcq-2026-8-28-fro-second-quarter-and-six-months-2026-results (same company, separate document).

findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the policy is public. The finding lands inside what the company told the market to expect.

findings.finding: The two 2017-built VLCCs sold in July for $270m (delivered August and September) give a Q3 gain on sale. It is below the line, lifts reported EPS above adjusted, and has no stated path to guidance.

findings.why_not_priced: Headline GAAP EPS will beat on it. The adjusted figure is the one that trades.

baseline_tension: The skew (+21.6, puts paid) and the -13.4% 20-day run-up both say downside. My evidence is roughly balanced: a telegraphed record Q4 against a spot correction and Hormuz tail risk. That neither strongly agrees with nor fights the skew, which is why p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (unsourced bar): no sourced street Q4 figure, so the next_guide finding was capped from +1.2 to +0.8.
Rule 7 (sign against strong skew): the expectations/sold-down finding goes against +21.6 put skew; shrunk from +0.8 to +0.6, and p_up moved 53 to 51.
Rule 2 (one-offs): gain on the VLCC sale cut from +0.1 to +0.05.
Lesson on untrustworthy FPI history: base rate rebuilt from confirmed releases (Q2 2026, Q1 2026, Q3 2025), all muted; abs_move cut from 5.0 to 4.5.
Rule 1 (fact is not reaction): already reflected in the draft via the peer reactions (DHT flat, Okeanis -0.3%); not applied twice.
